body:
ATTACK RESULTS — C-05 + pairing conflict

C-05 verdict: both gates are defensible only if `SUPPORTED` means public-eligible, never public. Applicant pp6-9 make verification necessary; p10 adds presenter/team approval; p11's <=5 s target is recommendation of <=3 items, not publication. Any copy/state that equates SUPPORTED with visible is a contradiction and a leak risk.

UX/failure attacks: (1) human approval has an unbounded tail, so publish-within-5s is impossible as an SLO; (2) presenter attention is the scarce resource—modals or forced decisions while speaking are unsafe; (3) a queued card may become stale/superseded or lose ACL/source validity before approval; (4) “team approval” is ambiguous (anyone/quorum/presenter override) and creates races; (5) three new cards every five seconds can flood the queue. Smallest resolution: one accountable approver—the active presenter/controller; team signals are advisory. Pre-render ranked cards, one tap/hotkey, no modal, ignore-to-expire, dedupe/cooldown, and version-check at approval.

Smallest defensible state machine is orthogonal rather than a cross-product:
- `verdict=PENDING|SUPPORTED|UNCERTAIN|CONFLICTING|UNSUPPORTED`
- `publication=HIDDEN|AWAITING_APPROVAL|PUBLISHED|REJECTED`
- `freshness=CURRENT|STALE|SUPERSEDED`
Start PENDING/HIDDEN/CURRENT. Only SUPPORTED+CURRENT that passes public classification/rights/privacy may enter AWAITING_APPROVAL. The active presenter approves by candidate ID; server rechecks exact revision/hash/ACL/classification/rights/DLP and atomically creates the public DTO. Slide/source/ACL change, expiry, or supersession blocks approval and retracts a published card. All other verdicts remain private. Never let the model/client submit audience JSON.

SLA correction: define p95 `utterance finalization -> eligible recommendation rendered in Presenter Console <=5s`; never include human decision. Separately target `approval accepted -> audience render <=300-500ms`. Partial STT may prefetch only; final STT triggers verification. Apply a hard verifier deadline, abstain/hold on timeout, and measure endpointing separately so the clock cannot be gamed. The existing 4.4s machine budget + 0.6s headroom is an engineering target requiring load test, not a guarantee.

Pairing verdict for the primary mirror case (QR is on a private, already authenticated setup console; anonymous mode out of MVP): account login on the new device IS mandatory. The 256-bit fragment “secret” is not acceptable evidence for a no-bearer-credential claim: RFC 3986 only proves fragments are separated before dereference; it does not protect QR photos, browser/extension/JS exposure, history-before-scrub, or redemption logs. If possession can authorize, it is still a bearer credential regardless of fragment placement.

Smallest safe flow: existing authenticated console creates a high-entropy opaque `pair_id`, one use, <=90s; QR contains only the transaction locator (fragment is fine for log minimization, but call it non-authorizing data). Phone scans, logs into the same authorized account if needed, and submits a pending device request bound server-side to account+device key+presentation+requested scopes. Existing console shows account/device/scopes and explicitly Approve/Deny. Approval atomically consumes pair_id and issues a new presentation-scoped opaque `__Host-` HttpOnly cookie to the phone; rotate/revoke at handoff/session end and assign WSS topics server-side. Possessing/photographing pair_id grants zero scope.

SAS decision: omit as a separate mandatory step in this private-QR + authenticated-account + explicit-existing-console-approval MVP; the approval is the trusted return channel. A short matching code can be shown inline as anti-misapproval defense, but becomes mandatory if QR can be audience-visible, anonymous pairing returns, or existing-console approval is removed. Do not retain the 256-bit fragment secret merely for entropy—the opaque pair_id already supplies unguessability without claiming bearer authority.

Evidence: RFC 8628 requires authenticated user review/approve and, for complete QR URIs, recommends displaying a matching code to mitigate remote phishing; it also identifies session spying. RFC 3986 §3.5 establishes fragment syntax/semantics only. OWASP LLM06 supports downstream authorization and human approval for high-impact actions.
summary: C-05 및 QR 페어링 공격 결론
